Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with ongoing right shoulder pain and reduced range
of motion. Over the course of 18 visits, care consisted of physical therapy, home exercise instruction, and as-needed
anti-inflammatory medication. Treatment followed an expected progression, with visit frequency tapering as
symptoms improved and function returned toward baseline. Examination findings were mixed: several provocative
maneuvers and range-of-motion measurements support a shoulder soft tissue injury, while strength testing and
neurological screening were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this
shoulder. Billed services reflect the planned course of care with no duplicate or repeated charges. At this time it
remains unclear to what extent the present complaints are attributable to the collision versus other causes, and
further imaging correlation may be helpful for that determination. Continued home exercise and reassessment are
recommended, with return precautions reviewed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
